additional_info.subject: ID0369734-DC/Si-D/FR[170002075&170001300] - Unavailable CRM:00315001601
additional_info.body:
Hello Ali, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
Do you have any trained technician to perform troubleshooting tasks?
From what I see, for the charger 1300, there seems to be a bad contact in the fuse, the error is triggering a lot of times and untriggering. From remote point of view it should be something as a loose wiring or the connector that needs to be verified. Also, there is a behavior where sometimes in the charger start up, the Main circuit breaker is not being switch on and only after 1 or 2 reboots it works again. For this I need to make some tests with visual aid from site to understand how the fuses and the inputs and outputs of the PLC cartridges are behaving.
For the charger 2075, there is a error flag pertaining to the DC plug's temperature sensor. The error is being activated and released a few seconds later, even when there is not a charging session. For this I would like, if you are able to do this, you to provide me a photo of the DC plug's condition, but I need a photo with the contacts/pins, just like the photo below:
If the DC plug looks good, then I believe that the input cables of the SECC might be loose or any connector not properly attached and can be fixed quickly.
Please let me know if I need to request the regional Siemens colleagues support to perform these troubleshootings.
Thank you very much and have a nice weekend!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: AutoRecharge - ID0369734-DC/Si-D/FR[170002075&170001300] - CableTempSensor & FB1 or FC5 tripping CRM:00315001617
additional_info.body:
Hello  colleagues
There are 2 chargers which have the following issues:
2075 → DC1_CableTempSensor
This error is occurring during non-charging hours, it seems like there is a loose contact to the StateMonitor, also it can be the cable, but it's hard to proactively look at the logs and understand what is happening in the EcoG since the error disappears after a few seconds.
Please check the connections from the cable to the XD10 and the input of the KF14.
1300 →
RCD_FB1_or_MCB_FC5_AC_Charging
One of the AC fuses is constantly tripping, it seems like there is also something wrong with either of these Fuses.
I recommend you to take spare parts to site for FC5 and FB1.
